evals.prompt: Review this 600-line PR diff for bugs and design problems. [diff that yields ~12 findings and several open questions]
expected_behavior: Writes every finding and question to the ledger, including per-item detail, before presenting any of them
Presents at most 3 open items, 2-4 lines each, with a marked default and what happens if deferred
Ends with the one-line footer (parked count, fyi count, ledger path) instead of listing the rest

evals.prompt: Help me plan migrating our monolith to services. [plan with many unknowns: team ownership, data split, cutover, auth]
expected_behavior: Recognizes that the response would contain more than 3 questions and uses the ledger instead of asking them inline
Ranks items that block other work first (e.g. data ownership before cutover order)
Logs low-stakes items as fyi with its own decision instead of asking the user

evals.prompt: (mid-triage; Q4 is irreversible and currently shown, Q5 is not) defaults all
expected_behavior: Accepts defaults for the reversible open and parked items and records each one in the ledger
Does NOT accept the default on the irreversible Q4; asks for an explicit answer
Closes or updates dependents settled by the accepted defaults

evals.prompt: (mid-triage) Q4 B, Q5 default, Q6 defer
expected_behavior: Records each resolution in the ledger (Q4's answer verbatim) before replying
Presents the next batch with no recap of the resolved items

evals.prompt: (new session after compaction; a .too-much/ ledger or a too-much beads epic exists) focus Q9
expected_behavior: Finds the existing ledger instead of saying there isn't one
Explains Q9 from its stored detail (evidence, options, what happens if deferred) without redoing the investigation

evals.prompt: (mid-triage, while fixing F3) this makes me wonder whether we need rate limiting at all
expected_behavior: Adds the rate-limiting question to the ledger as parked instead of asking it inline
Continues the current batch unless the new item blocks it

evals.prompt: (in a repo with .beads/ and a working bd) too much, triage this
expected_behavior: Uses beads: one parent epic labeled too-much, one child per item with type and irreversible labels and a priority
Records resolutions with bd close --reason, using the user's words verbatim
Picks the next batch with bd ready --parent, excluding parked items
